decisions.reason: Its dedicated product page in both 2023 and 2024 suggests results are at least near aspiration levels, and a large established firm has enough slack to continue backing it.
The successful ESA HERA launch is a clear positive market signal above aspiration, so management would strongly favor retaining it.
Continued standalone presentation in 2024 indicates the product remains strategically relevant, and absent clear failure the firm would keep it while learning more.
Being only mentioned rather than prominently presented in both years points to weaker traction versus aspiration, making resource reallocation to stronger space optics projects more likely.
As a 2024 launch with its own page, it is too early for harsh evaluation and organizational slack supports keeping it on the market for another year.
Its low-profile 2024 mention suggests uncertainty, but as a very new and strategically related space product it would likely be retained for one more evaluation period.
